plan: Economic theory suggests the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my private value of $27. This eliminates the risk of bidding too low and losing the auction, or bidding too high and potentially losing money. Since values are independently drawn each round, there's no historical information to adjust my strategy. Bidding my true value maximizes my expected profit by ensuring I win when the prize is worth more than the second-highest bid.

Economic theory suggests the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my private value of $31. In a first-price sealed bid auction, bidding less risks losing the item, while bidding more risks negative earnings. Since values are independently and randomly drawn each round, there's no strategic advantage to deviating from a "bid your value" approach. I will bid my full private value to maximize my potential profit.

Economic theory suggests bidding exactly at my private value ($20) is the dominant strategy in a second-price sealed bid auction. This eliminates the risk of overbidding and ensures I maximize potential profit. Since values are independently drawn and this is a single round, strategic complexity is reduced. I'll bid precisely at my true value, which prevents potential losses from bidding too high or missing out by bidding too low.
